data.title: Fear and broken families: Inside a Texas ICE detention centre
data.description: Since Donald Trump’s return to the White House in January 2025, migrant arrests have surged in the United States. More than 610,000 people have passed through detention centres run by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), the federal immigration agency in under two years. The pace only continues to accelerate: in August 2026, nearly 51,000 arrests were made in a single month – a record for Trump’s second term. Who are the people being held in these centres? What are their living conditions like? And how is Trump’s mass deportation policy upending the lives of families settled in the United States? In this report, Valérie Defert and Pierrick Laurent investigate the issue in Texas – the heart of the new US immigration detention system.

data.title: 'Election without meaningful competition': Russia’s results won't measure support for Putin or war
data.description: Alison Sargent is pleased to welcome Grégoire Roos, Director of the Europe and Russia and Eurasia Programmes at Chatham House. According to Roos, Russia’s parliamentary election is revealing because of what the electoral process can still tell us about the political system Vladimir Putin has constructed. In the absence of any meaningful competition, and anti-war opposition excluded, Roos argues that the most revealing signals may lie elsewhere: in turnout, the timing of voting, the performance of the remaining parties, and the Kremlin’s effort to frame participation itself as evidence of national unity.

data.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome investigative journalist Emanuel Maiberg, Co-founder of 404 Media. As we embark on AI's uncharted waters, Maiberg has made a most unexpected discovery:: the mass acquisition, dismemberment and scanning of rare books for use as training data. data.title: ‘A map is never neutral’: meet the cartographers who took on centuries of western bias
data.description: Equal Earth projection, adopted by the UN last week, provides an alternative to 16th-century Mercator display Three cartographers have spoken of their astonishment at the UN’s near-universal adoption of a map they created to more accurately show the sizes of Africa and Europe, even though they have received a few complaints from some disgruntled diplomats. The creators of the Equal Earth projection aimed to provide an alternative to the dominant 16th-century Mercator display, which critics have long faulted for giving the impression that northern hemisphere nations are larger than they are – and therefore subtly reinforcing perceptions of where global strength lies. data.title: ‘The damage was much worse than I had imagined’: the shocking inside story of Salman Rushdie’s survival
data.description: After ​the writer was stabbed in a horrific attack, his wife started making a video diary of his recovery. The clips are featured in a new film from Alex Gibney, who drew on Dennis Potter to create a powerful portrait of Rushdie’s tumultuous life Eliza Griffiths was at home in New York, drinking a second cup of coffee one August morning in 2022, when her phone rang. She answered it to a frantic friend, who told her the man she had married just a year earlier, and who had set off the previous night for a speaking engagement nearly 400 miles away, had been hurt. “What kind of hurt?” she panicked. Turning on the television, she was assaulted by blurry images of chaos on stage as audience members surged to the rescue. Her husband, Sir Salman Rushdie, had been stabbed multiple times and was fighting for his life. Within days of desperately chartering a plane to fly her to Rushdie’s hospital bedside, not knowing if he was alive or dead, Griffiths – a poet and photographer who works under her full name Rachel Eliza Griffiths – had begun to make a video diary recording his treatment and recovery. “When it had become likely that I was going to survive,” says Rushdie drily, “I said to Eliza we need to make a record of this. By which I meant something very modest: maybe she would take a picture of me on her iPhone every couple of days just to document the recovery, but Eliza had bigger ideas.” Continue reading...

data.title: The spectre of ‘remigration’ is haunting Europe. Slovenia in 1992 gives us a blueprint for this state terror | Miha Mazzini
data.description: In February that year, the Slovenian government officially deleted 25,000 citizens, turning them overnight into illegal immigrants So much of your daily life – your job, your health, your home – hinges on the fact that your name is in a government database. Are you a legal citizen of your country, with everything that entails? You are, until an anonymous bureaucrat hits a key one night and strips it all away, turning you into an illegal immigrant. It happened in Slovenia in 1992. “I took my son to register for secondary school. The clerk rifled through the papers, then stared at me as if refusing to see the boy standing right next to me. Finally, she said: ‘But you don’t have a son. He doesn’t exist.’” I can’t forget the look on the face of the woman who was telling me this story. It was a mixture of deep hurt and bewilderment, with a pause after every sentence, as if she were walking through a minefield. During the research for my book Erased, I compiled countless stories like this: stories I once would have thought impossible. Miha Mazzini is a writer, film-maker and anthropologist Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? If you would like to submit a response of up to 300 words by email to be considered for publication in our letters section, please click here . Continue reading...

data.title: Experience: I survived being buried in an avalanche
data.description: I was at the mercy of the mountain, heading towards a 20-metre drop, about to discover what it felt like to die Growing up in Sweden, I was as comfortable on skis as I was walking on my feet. As a teenager, I became a professional free skier, a style that features jumps and tricks. In my 20s, I moved into content creation. Now, at 38, I spend the winter months filming extreme ski videos with my photographer wife, Sofia. In March this year, we’d been staying at the base of the Lyngen Alps, northern Norway. Nonstop rain had prevented us from filming but, finally, we had fresh powder and clear skies. The plan was for me to go up the mountain with a friend, Lovisa, and make our way down as the sun was setting. Sofia would film us from the bottom using a drone. Continue reading...

data.title: MobLand season two review – why is Pierce Brosnan’s tedious crime drama so obsessed with testicle jokes?
data.description: This Guy-Ritchie-directed gangland drama is deathly dull. It’s a charm-free watch with awful characters and humour so genital-based that at one point Helen Mirren yells a penis joke at a sausage MobLand. It sounds like a regional nightclub. Or a boyband. But it’s not. It’s a Paramount+ crime drama starring Pierce Brosnan as an Irishman unable to speak in a convincing Irish accent. This is his tragedy. His cross to bear. And now it’s ours, too, because MobLand is back for a second series, with Brosnan – as the veteran gang boss Conrad Harrigan – once again battling other gang bosses while attempting to say things like “Oi love ye loike a tramp loves paraffin” without his vowels shrivelling into tiny raisins of pseudo-Hibernian shame. Does he succeed? Oi tink not! But there are bigger problems afoot, to be sure. Created by Ronan “Top Boy” Bennett and directed by Guy Ritchie, the first series of the London-set MobLand (feel the width of that capitalised L!) was a sustained roar of nothing much; a rumble through every possible modern gangster drama cliche in the Every Modern Gangster Drama Cliche book. You know the sort of thing: car chases through suspiciously empty city streets; convoluted drug deals with mumbling eastern Europeans; tiny-eyed endomorphs in flat caps bellowing “Oi” in slow motion as they hurtle through the air to the strains of something unconscionable by Kasabian. Continue reading...

data.title: No hope, no vote … how most of Delhi’s sex workers are being struck off electoral rolls
data.description: Modi’s bid to ‘purify’ voter lists has affected a third of the city’s residents. In the GB Road red light district, those who lack permanent homes and documents are among the hardest hit Rows of hardware and car-part shops line Garstin Bastion Road, with faded signs crammed together above their shutters. By day, the street is one of Old Delhi’s busiest commercial thoroughfares. But as dusk falls, GB Road, as it is known locally, transforms into one of the city’s most notorious red-light districts. An estimated 2,800 sex workers live and work in brothels that occupy the upper floors of the dilapidated buildings, their entrances tucked behind narrow stairways and unmarked doors. Women sit on plastic stools beneath the stairways, calling out to men passing on the street, while others watch from windows above, their eyes following the movement below before customers are directed upstairs. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Like a Bond villain’s lair’: I climbed the Dolomites to the world’s most spectacular mountain hut
data.description: Perched above the clouds in northern Italy, Santnerpass refuge doesn’t just look stunning. It’s a marvel of eco-building – and vegetarian cuisine ‘I think my boots are falling apart!” shouts Nigel just as we hit the pinnacles, a whole range of them jutting up and out from the mountainside, all thrillingly tall, spiky and knobbled. Through them we painstakingly step, fingers aching in gloves, heads sweating in helmets – squashing up narrow chimneys, squeezing through mighty boulders and inching along slender ledges on a twisting path that’s only just discernible through swathes of sharp white scree. I know how Nigel’s boots are feeling: the going is far harder than I was expecting. This is only the first day of our annual trip to the Dolomites, a vast range of breathtaking sawtooth peaks in northern Italy, but my head’s already full of the thought I have every year as we start out: “If only you’d got fitter.” Continue reading...

data.title: Think it’s time for gen Z to ‘grow up’? You’re even more out of touch than the British state | Gaby Hinsliff
data.description: We can’t expect young people to make a seamless transition from childhood to adulthood in this chilly economic climate. Finally, Westminster is catching on When did you realise you had finally grown up? It’s a trick question, obviously: maturity is just realising that life is full of things you don’t feel old enough for but somehow manage anyway, while getting better at pretending to know what you’re doing. But the question is worth asking nonetheless, because for gen Z the goalposts of grownup life are clearly shifting. It’s a truism that adulting now comes later than it did to generations who still don’t consider adulting a verb, with 43% of 25-year-olds still living at home and plenty more jobless university graduates boomeranging back there this summer, thanks to a grim labour market. Since they’ll probably be working longer into what were once retirement years, perhaps it’s only natural that they’re taking longer to get started. But there’s a fine line between choosing to grow up more slowly and becoming trapped into a kind of limbo between childhood and adulthood, with nobody to pull you out of the morass beyond parents who aren’t sure how to handle this new life stage either. Gaby Hinsliff is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: Watching NAZA was like peering through a window – and seeing the machinery of killing in Gaza | Mahmoud Mushtaha
data.description: For so long I wondered why I survived while family and friends were killed. Now I know the only difference between life and death may have been an AI algorithm The lights go down, and for a moment I forget I’m watching a screen. It fills with a rooftop in Tel Aviv at night, black and grey. The camera pans down. Through windows, we see people watching screens of their own – couples holding each other close, following the news, eating food. They appear absorbed in their own worlds, and why wouldn’t they be? That’s the thing I can’t get past as a Palestinian journalist from Gaza, watching this apparent tranquillity: this must be it – this must be what safety actually looks like. Just an evening uninterrupted, with no military aircraft flying overhead or drones buzzing incessantly. Meanwhile, men and women on the rooftop above them calmly talk about how they decided how many Palestinian civilians would die on any given night. Mahmoud Mushtaha is a Palestinian journalist from Gaza, and the author of Sobrevivir al genocidio en Gaza (Surviving the Genocide in Gaza). This article is based on a piece first published in +972 Magazine . Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? Good job he wasn’t part of a Treasury team that abolished the Office for Tax Simplification On days like this, it’s not hard to be overwhelmed by existential futility. At the current rate of progress, the UK looks on course to wipe itself out far sooner than it would with any interference from AI. Everything feels hopeless. Years of minimal growth and a cost of living crisis. The tech bros and the bankers may be getting richer. The rest of us? Not so much. And there’s no end in sight. Andy Burnham may offer better vibes, but he is fighting a losing battle against global forces – wars, energy prices, borrowing costs – that he can’t control. All the economic forecasts suggest things are going to get even worse in the next year. Continue reading...

data.title: Trump says the US doesn’t need Canada. But it’s the source of key minerals for the military | Vince Beiser
data.description: Trump himself has acknowledged the US need for Canadian aluminum – and has largely exempted metals from new tariffs As trade talks with Canada shambled toward collapse in late August, Donald Trump brayed on Truth Social: “WE DON’T NEED CANADA, THEY NEED US!” But in fact, Canada, like China, has something the US needs badly: critical metals that undergird modern military technology. Canada is the United States’s biggest foreign source of minerals, supplying about $47bin worth each year. Sixty per cent of all the aluminum the US uses each year, for instance, comes from Canada, where mighty, remote rivers provide smelting plants vast quantities of cheap, low-carbon electricity. The US military uses the lightweight metal for everything from shell casings to ship hulls and aircraft fuselage. The Pentagon’s cutting-edge F-35 fighter jet’s airframe is about 40% aluminum. “This country desperately needs aluminum,” Trump complained last month . “We get it all from Canada for the most part, and we need it badly.” Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on EU-Canada relations: strategic ambition with lessons for Britain | Editorial
data.description: Mark Carney’s response to the challenges posed by an unreliable US president contains a clarity of vision that is lacking in post-Brexit Britain There is no “associate membership” of the European Union, nor any blueprint for what such a thing might involve. It is a political hypothesis, describing a relationship of intimate strategic alignment with the EU, stopping short of actual membership, in ways that are significant but undefined. This week, Ursula von der Leyen, the European Commission president, invited Canada to be the first country to enjoy this putative status. In her state of the union speech, she spoke of a future relationship elevated “to the highest level possible”, reflecting an affinity of interests and values. Mark Carney, the Canadian prime minister, reciprocated the sentiment in a speech on Wednesday. Addressing the European parliament, he said the two sides should secure “strategic autonomy through deep cooperation” across a broad spectrum of interests: trade, defence, industrial capacity, science, space and AI. He proposed Canadian participation in the EU’s Erasmus student exchange programme and Horizon research scheme. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: The Guardian view on the Nepal-Tibet floods: a spur to action on climate | Editorial
data.description: New research links last month’s disaster to fossil fuel pollution. Supporting disaster-hit countries must be at the centre of climate politics Following a familiar pattern, coverage of the glacier collapse on the Nepal-Tibet border three weeks ago has subsided with the initial shock. But while the world’s attention has shifted, Nepal remains in the midst of an appalling tragedy. As well as at least 1,300 people who are known to have been killed, more than 5,000 are missing, some of them trapped in tunnels linked to the 13 hydropower plants that were damaged by the floods. On Wednesday four bodies were recovered from one of these tunnels, with searches ongoing. Families of the missing people are desperate for news. Last week the country’s foreign minister, Shisir Khanal, said that it would ask the UN’s loss and damage fund for $20m (£15m) towards a total rebuilding cost of around $5bn (£3.75bn) – including the replacement of up to 20,000 homes. The first academic study linking the disaster to the climate crisis will now be added to that application. data.title: Todd Boehly exits Chelsea diminished after having his fingers burned
data.description: The billionaire’s departure will change little day-to-day but could be significant for club’s stadium plans Not since a doomed foray into the thorny world of the transfer market has Todd Boehly had any real influence over the day-to-day at Chelsea. The American exits football as a diminished figure four years on, along with his fellow investor Mark Walter, and the first thing to say is that little will change in the Stamford Bridge boardroom just because Boehly has left the scene. Clearlake Capital, the US private equity firm founded by Behdad Eghbali and José E Feliciano, was already the majority owner and guiding force. The trio of Boehly, Walter and the Swiss billionaire Hansjörg Wyss had an equal share of a 38.5% stake but have drifted into irrelevance since the BlueCo consortium bought Chelsea from Roman Abramovich for £2.5bn in 2022. data.title: Chess: Nigel Short to play at south pole in event criticised over climate impact
data.description: The former world title challenger, 61, will take on representatives from five other continents in a tournament rated by the global chess body Fide Nigel Short, the 1993 world title challenger, will head to the Antarctic for his next tournament as the 61-year-old, formerly of Bolton but resident for many decades in Greece, attempts to become the first chess player to win tournaments on seven continents. There is history for the very strongest grandmasters successfully defying the ravages of time: Emanuel Lasker in his mid-60s at Moscow 1935 and 1936, Viktor Korchnoi in his seventies, and, most impressive of all, Vasily Smyslov reaching the 1984 Candidates final against Garry Kasparov at 63. data.title: Europa League roundup: Ferencvaros pile more misery on troubled Celtic
data.description: Hoops beaten again after chastening loss to Rangers Juventus hammer NEC, Besiktas pile woe on Marseille Celtic suffered another European embarrassment as the Scottish champions were beaten 3-1 at home by Ferencvaros in the Europa League. Just weeks on from crashing out of the Champions League qualifiers to the Austrian side Lask, despite at one point holding a four-goal lead, Celtic’s defensive flaws were exposed once more. Martin O’Neill’s team also suffered a chastening 3-0 defeat by their rivals Rangers in the League Cup last weekend and failed to deliver on their manager’s promise to respond, with a home league derby against the Gers looming. Bamidele Yusuf opened the scoring for the visitors before Mika Baur equalised late in the first half. However, Kristoffer Zachariassen quickly put Ferencvaros back in front before Daniel Arzani’s sensational strike, on his return to Celtic Park, capped a fine night for Ferencvaros. Continue reading...

data.title: Sydney Sweeney’s cartoonish provocation has sparked a culture war but let’s just admit sport can be sexy | Emma John
data.description: Yes sport is about effort, sweat and inclusivity – but it also turns elite athletes into magnificent specimens of humanity where the aesthetic is part of the appeal Have you seen the 40-second video that will change the way you think about women’s sport, women’s bodies, just, you know, women? It’s been unavoidable on social media this week – brazen, unapologetic, dominating the algorithm like an AI kitten hacking a banana-bread recipe while lip-syncing to Cardi B. I for one have enjoyed it at least 50 times already. It starts with some carefully curated passive-aggression – “Dear Sydney”, “Hey Sydney”, “Respectfully Sydney” – and follows up with clips of what, in its own words, “a woman in sport actually looks like”. It shows its subject pounding the treadmill or powering down the back straight, flooring a rival with a tackle or a roundhouse kick, lifting weights or throwing herself through the air. It is, inevitably, soundtracked by Dua Lipa. Training Season is getting a serious bump this week. Continue reading...

data.title: Robert Kraft, once the NFL’s good guy, is just another billionaire silencing Macklemore | Howard Bryant
data.description: The Patriots owner’s decision to ban the rapper from performing at the team’s stadium brings back memories of the blackballing of Colin Kaepernick Six years ago, in the middle of a “racial reckoning” that never was, a White House that had begun out of control reached its chaotic apex. Federal officials were sweeping citizens off American streets in unmarked vehicles , surrounding the Lincoln Memorial with armed guards and rolling military vehicles through residential neighborhoods in a fascist reaction to protests against the murder of George Floyd. It was at this point that NFL commissioner Roger Goodell, realizing it had all gone too far, appeared on a Zoom and admitted his league was “wrong” for not listening to its players when they had protested against police brutality. The implication was clear: more than any other sports league, the NFL was harshest in its reaction to the protests that began with Trayvon Martin in 2012 and continued with Ferguson, Baltimore and Colin Kaepernick. By blackballing Kaepernick, sitting by while broadcast partners refused to air the national anthem to undermine the protests, and, most embarrassingly, Goodell’s draconian announcement that teams would be subject to fines if players showed dissent, the NFL had proven itself to act in the most un-American of ways. Howard Bryant is the author of 11 books, including Full Dissidence: Notes from an Uneven Playing Field, and Kings and Pawns: Jackie Robinson and Paul Robeson in America. He also writes on Substack Continue reading...

data.title: The world’s rivers are at breaking point. Can we save them before it is too late?
data.description: In this week’s newsletter: As the Guardian launches a year-long project, Our Rivers, we take stock of the issues facing waterways around the world Don’t get Down to Earth delivered to your inbox? Sign up here The nicknames of the world’s biggest rivers give a sense of how we feel about them: “the great river”, “the river that swallows all rivers”, “Mother Ganga” and “Old father Thames”. They feed and water us, and many other animal species. They carry our trade but also give us cool relief on a hot day. They’re nerve endings, elders and sources of comfort, but also of awe and respect. And yet many of the world’s rivers are suffering, hit by multiple environmental challenges. A new report out today from the World Meteorological Organization finds that rivers across the world experienced one of the driest years in more than three decades during 2025. data.title: New cat species identified for first time in more than a century in Bolivia
data.description: New species of wild feline was discovered in Bolivia’s Yungas forest that is smaller than the average domestic ⁠cat A diminutive wild cat that inhabits Bolivia’s ⁠cloud forest has been identified as a previously unknown species, marking the first time a new living feline species has been formally named and described in more than a century. The cat, called tilcayo by local communities, is part of a group called tiger ⁠cats found across much of South ⁠America. It was found in Bolivia’s ​lush Yungas forest, a mountainous region where forests are often covered by clouds and surrounded by high humidity, according to researchers. It measures about 18in (46cm) long and weighs about 3lb (1.4kg), making it smaller than the average domestic ⁠cat. Continue reading...

data.title: Trump officials move to dismantle key protection for US endangered species
data.description: Fish and Wildlife Service memo calls for change in what it means to ‘take’ an endangered species More than 1,600 critically imperiled species protected under the US Endangered Species Act (ESA) face losing further federal protections following a new reinterpretation of the 1973 law by the Donald Trump administration. A September 14 memo distributed to Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) field offices by FWS director Brian Nesvik calls for a reinterpretation of what it means to “take” an endangered species. Under the ESA , “take” is defined as “to harass, harm, pursue, hunt, shoot, wound, kill, trap, capture, or collect, or to attempt to engage in any such conduct”. Continue reading...

Adding their voices to demands that the prime minister takes public control of the company, which has debts of £20bn and is being controlled by a group of 100 hedge funds and distressed-debt investors, the MPs said in a report that ministers should consider emergency legislation to take control of its financial affairs to stabilise the company. data.title: Find a credible plan for British Steel, ministers told as ‘startling’ costs soar
data.description: Government spending watchdog warns of price of keeping publicly owned firm in business Labour has been urged to lay out a credible plan for the future of British Steel, as the government spending watchdog warned of the “startling” costs of keeping the struggling manufacturer in business with no end in sight. British Steel was taken into public ownership in July to protect “the future of steel production”, 15 months after the government stepped in to prevent the closure of its steelworks in Scunthorpe and the loss of 4,000 jobs. data.title: Addison Lee founder owes £20.5m in tax after UK tribunal ruling
data.description: HMRC wins challenge over John Griffin’s claim to be non-dom despite having lived in England since childhood The founder of Addison Lee owes £20.5m in tax after a tribunal dismissed a claim that he should be treated as a nom-dom despite living in the UK since childhood. John Griffin had argued he should be treated as a nom-dom due to his connection to Ireland, saying: “I was and am besotted with Ireland, infatuated with Ireland. I believe that I have always been and am Irish.” Continue reading...

data.description: The gift from Italy has sparked fierce debate among defence analysts and opposition politicians who question its true cost and purpose Indonesia has received its first aircraft carrier, a former Italian warship that the government says will strengthen the archipelagic nation’s maritime security and disaster response capabilities. The 41-year-old former ITS Giuseppe Garibaldi, with capacity for short takeoff and vertical landing aircraft and helicopters, arrived Friday morning at a naval base in North Jakarta’s Tanjung Priok port, where it was welcomed with a military ceremony. data.title: New lawsuit alleges Epstein possessed ‘child sexual abuse material of countless children’
data.description: Two women who filed suit against Epstein estate ask court to order program to notify potential victims Jeffrey Epstein ’s estate is facing a new lawsuit filed by two women who allege that Epstein possessed child sexual abuse material (CSAM) of them. They want a judge to order that a program be set up to identify and notify all individuals whose “unlawful sexualized images” might have been in Epstein’s collection, and are also seeking monetary damages. The complaint was filed this week in the US district court for the southern district of New York on behalf of two plaintiffs, who are anonymous in the filing but described as survivors of Epstein’s CSAM crimes. The lawsuit was filed against Epstein’s former lawyer Darren Indyke and Epstein’s former accountant Richard Kahn , who are being sued in their capacities as co-executors of Epstein’s estate. Attorneys for Indyke and Kahn, who have both said that they had no knowledge of Epstein’s crimes during their employment, did not immediately respond to a request for comment about the complaint on Wednesday. Continue reading...

data.title: No Land to Stand On by Mahmoud Khalil review – a searing account of political imprisonment
data.description: The Palestinian Columbia student snatched by ICE writes about his Kafkaesque ordeal with a quiet fury Mahmoud Khalil was completing a master’s degree at Columbia University when, in March 2025, plain-clothed officers from the Department of Homeland Security snatched him from his home in New York and took him to an immigration detention centre; he was then transferred to another facility in Louisiana, more than 1,000 miles away. As a green card holder, Khalil has permanent US residency, but secretary of state Marco Rubio had determined that his continued presence in the country would have “adverse foreign policy consequences for the United States”, and sought his deportation under a legal provision dating back to the McCarthy era. Khalil was released on bail in June 2024 after a federal judge ruled his detention unconstitutional, but the Trump administration is still trying to have him removed. Khalil – who was born to Palestinian parents in a refugee camp in Syria – had been targeted because of his advocacy on behalf of pro-Palestinian protesters during campus protests over Columbia University’s links to Israel. They were calling for Columbia to cut its ties with Israeli academic institutions and companies profiting from Israel’s onslaught on Gaza; in response, the university called in the NYPD. There was no suggestion that Khalil had done anything unlawful, and no criminal charges were brought against him; the government had simply identified him as an influential pro-Palestinian voice on campus, and for that reason alone they wanted him gone. He spent a total of 104 days in detention, missing the birth of his son. Continue reading...

data.title: Pulp: What Do You Do for an Encore? review – Jarvis Cocker’s wit and warmth upstage the hits
data.description: Wonderful archive footage charts the Sheffield outsiders’ unlikely rise, but the distant camerawork struggles to capture the thrill of their triumphant O2 gigs In 1978, in the classroom of a comprehensive school in Sheffield, a skinny, shortsighted 15-year-old wrote a mission statement in the back of an exercise book – a masterplan for reaching the top with the band he had recently formed with some classmates who, like him, weren’t picked first for sports. In 2023, after a hiatus of a decade, his band Pulp started touring again, and last year played to 20,000 people at each of two nights at the O2 in London. This film features concert footage from those gigs in which a still lithe, still-got-it-at-60-odd Jarvis Cocker sings his hit art-pop anthems backed by most of the classic lineup and a 10-piece string section. And interspersed with the concert footage are autobiographical musings, nostalgic archive footage, interviews with Jarvis’s mum and gran, and Cocker narrating the story of how he got from there, almost half a century ago, to here. Continue reading...

data.title: Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story review – it’s like Ryan Murphy’s new series was written by adolescent boys
data.description: The latest Monster instalment, about the 1892 Borden axe murders, is packed with periods and beheadings, and feels like it was made up as they went along Okaaay – here’s what I think must have happened. Some time in the past year or two, Ryan Murphy discovered that women menstruate. Incredulous but enthralled, he rushed off to share the news with his soon equally incredulous and enthralled little friends. After confirming the basics they all looked at each other for a moment in silence as they contemplated this crazy, secret habit of the wimminz. And then Ryan said: “You guys? We have got to make a show about this!” The others nodded in fervent agreement and off they all ran. The result is the utterly bonkers, blood-soaked, borderline-fetishistic fever dream that is The Lizzie Borden Story – the latest entry in Murphy’s popular anthology series Monster. This one is written by Ian Brennan and directed in the main by Max Winkler, the pairing responsible for the series’ previous offering, last year’s lamentable The Ed Gein Story. As, I presume, a gesture to the sex of this one’s subject, there is a female director for two of the Lizzie Borden episodes – Sarah Adina Smith – but it doesn’t really dent the vibe. Think: the gleeful disgust of a roomful of adolescent boys being taught about the female reproductive system in PSHE. It is now an eight-hour miniseries starring Rebecca Hall. We live in strange times. Continue reading...

data.title: Best of the Best review – college comedy formula gets a Bollywood makeover
data.description: What’s engaging in this tale of two best girl friends and a dance competition is not the familiar plot but the whip-fast telling and brilliant choreograpy There is absolutely nothing unexpected about this Netflix comedy set in the world of rival Bollywood dance groups on American campuses. Each plot twist is instantly familiar, every character recognisable, the essential formula untweaked from a dozen previous college comedies. But it’s funny and snappy, and directed with infectious energy by Lena Khan, one of the few Muslim female film-makers working in Hollywood. The scriptwriters are Hasan Minhaj and Prashanth Venkataramanujam, a pair of millennial comedians who look as if they’ve done enough research on the inner workings of gen Z behaviour to write a PhD. Maya (Maitreyi Ramakrishnan) and Anjali (Priyanka Kedia) star as lifelong best friends who enrol together at UCLA. Maya is the clever difficult one; Anjali is the nice pretty one. (It goes without saying Maya is also a total babe.) During freshers’ week they join the college’s Bollywood dance club where, predictably, Maya locks horns with leader Ronak (Ankur Rathee) over the choreography. He wants to base their new-season routine on Bollywood weddings, which, as Maya points out, is a bit trad. If they are going to beat their rivals they will need to come up with something modern and fresh. Continue reading...

data.title: Baka Beyond: Sing the World Awake review – powerful Cameroonian vocals burst through fussy arrangements
data.description: (March Hare Music) This fusion of western folk and the traditional music of the Baka people creates an uneven patchwork of sound – but it astonishes when their vocals are placed front and centre Over the past 30 years, British folk musicians Su Hart and Martin Cradick have been developing a distinct fusion of traditional Cameroonian vocal music with western instrumentation. Their 1993 debut record Spirits of the Forest, released on Joe Boyd’s Hannibal Records, focused on the female singers of the Baka people, who use a polyphonic style of yodelling to evoke dawn spirits. Hart and Cradick have maintained the relationship over the decades, splitting royalties equally and supporting the community through their Global Music Exchange charity. Sing the World Awake, their first album in 12 years, centres field recordings made with a new Baka generation and deepens their exploration into an ancient oral tradition. Cradick’s instrumental arrangements are expansive and wide-ranging. Topé Malangui Kpode features sprightly, Ghanaian highlife-inspired guitar melodies and percussive polyrhythms. Fair Molly (Mál Bhán Ní Chuilleanáin) features Gaelic vocals from guest singer Irene O’Meara, and The Swift harnesses the intricate folk sound of Ben Moneypenny’s violin playing. Each song alights on snatches of Baka vocals, although the overall effect of splicing these unique melodies into different genres creates an uneven patchwork of sound. Continue reading...

data.title: Exaudi: Pocket Universe album review – virtuoso vocals with a joyfully bonkers bent
data.description: Exaudi/Weeks (NMC) Four substantial, eclectic works written for James Weeks’ ensemble are brought together here, encompassing swooping folk phrasing, delicate harmonising and exuberant stylistic skill There is a lot of joy in this release from Exaudi and their conductor, James Weeks, bringing together four substantial, eclectic works written for the vocal group during the 2010s. The first is Guide by Cassandra Miller . Based on a devotional song as recorded in 1968 by the folk singer Maria Muldaur, phrases of which are repeated freely by the singers in imitation of Muldaur’s swooping, full-voiced style, it builds quickly into a kind of controlled cacophony. Andrew Hamilton ’s Proclamation of the Republic imagines Patrick Pearse outside the Dublin General Post Office at Easter 1916, reading the historic text to a largely confused or oblivious public; little by little, pairing syllables on a quietly but insistently repeating two-note figure, the music blooms into something that seems to unite the crowd as they walk away, humming. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘You think you’re done and you get pigeonholed’: Samantha Morton on raving, Richard Russell and having another shot as a singer
data.description: The actor and musician spoke at our Guardian Live ‘Honest Playlist’ event at Green Man festival about growing up in Nottingham on the free-party scene, and the healing powers of music On the Sunday afternoon of Green Man Festival in August, Samantha Morton joined me onstage in the Talking Shop tent to discuss her life in music. The celebrated actor and director is currently in cinemas as the scene-stealing Circe in The Odyssey , but she is also a musician. Later that day, she performed on the main stage later with Everything Is Recorded, the supergroup led by XL label boss Richard Russell, who also collaborated with Morton on her 2024 solo album Daffodils & Dirt . More recently, she voiced her character’s title song on The Odyssey soundtrack. “I love talking about music,” she says. “I never really get asked enough to talk about music.” For this in-depth conversation with Guardian Live, Morton took us through her Honest Playlist of songs on various themes that have meant something to her, including the first single she bought, Musical Youth’s reggae-pop hit Pass The Dutchie, the song she’d do at karaoke, Michael Prophet and Ricky Tuffy’s Your Love, and a great song to fall in love to (Moments In Love by Art of Noise). She thinks about playlists often, revealing that she makes them whenever she needs to get into character for a role and used to “carry tapes in my back pocket everywhere I went because I couldn’t have bad music.” Continue reading...

data.title: My Year in Paris With Gertrude Stein by Deborah Levy audiobook review – gripping vision of a fearless writer
data.description: A fictional British author in Paris sets out to explore Stein through the lens of her own friendships, in this inventive, perfectly paced portrait It is late 2024, and an unnamed British author living in Paris is trying to write an essay on Gertrude Stein, the modernist writer and art collector. The author has been distracted by her friend Eva’s cat, who is lost and whose name is “it” in lower case, which inevitably leads to confusion – has Eva lost her cat or her mind? (Her other friend, Fanny, has rechristened the cat Bob, to make talking about him easier.) The Pennsylvania-born Stein was painted by Picasso, hung out with Hemingway and wrote strange, stream-of-consciousness prose long before James Joyce embarked on his masterwork Ulysses. Commercial success didn’t come until she was in her 60s with The Autobiography of Alice B Toklas, a biography of her partner and one of her more accessible books. Our narrator is an admirer of Stein’s work, yet she can be exasperated by it. “Sometimes, when I read her baffling and beguiling writing I want to smack it in the chops. [Stein] longed for her readers to find her, yet there was a part of her that could not bear to be found.” Continue reading...

data.title: Feeling overwhelmed by the AI doom loop? Here’s the essential reading list to make sense of it all
data.description: It’s a chaotic time in an industry that’s reshaping our lives – Guardian reporters and experts recommend the books that help explain how we got here, and where we’re heading Have you been feeling trapped in an endless cycle of artificial intelligence hype and panic? You’re not alone. It’s a chaotic time to make sense of the industry that’s reshaping our lives, whether or not we like it. Last week, another AI company employee publicly resigned , warning the technology “could kill us all by the end of the decade”. data.title: Beck: ‘What does a devil’s haircut look like? Anything with a lot of architecture and wild flights of fancy’
data.description: The genre-fluid singer answers your questions on being funky v lonesome, his infamous MTV interview with Thurston Moore and why he said yes to performing with a chain-smoking alcoholic robot • Read Alexis Petridis’s 5* review of new album Ride Lonesome You’ve been performing since the late 80s. What keeps you going? AmongstTheWaves It’s a good question. I don’t really know any other life. I’ve spent a lot of my time trying to create a body of work, and out of that, maybe there’s a few songs at the end that are not bad. So I just keep going down into the mine, trying to come back with a couple of things worth keeping. It’s a lot of digging. If I had to stop and get a job painting houses or something, I would still make songs just for myself, because that’s how it started. You tend to alternate between styles from album to album. What do you feel is closer to your intrinsic self, funky Beck or lonesome Beck ? Mazzini Probably lonesome. But the other side of things gets me out of my shell, stops me from being a little too ponderous, which I’m apt to do. The other side of what I do – Loser or Odelay – was more of a fluke. At the time that was what people liked. Now it’s kind of reversed – they prefer the more introspective, quiet songs, and stuff that’s a little more genreless. I don’t have any songs that they play at weddings, like Uptown Funk. I remember telling Mark Ronson, “Hey, you made a wedding song.” He was like, “Yeah, finally.” That’s a very elite category of song. Continue reading...

data.title: Why did a high-profile fashion CEO physically restrain Peta protesters at New York fashion week?
data.description: Steven Kolb tried to stop activists demonstrating against the use of wool – but he can’t curb consumers’ growing concern about where their clothes come from On Sunday afternoon, Mason Melito took a front row seat at the Cos show at New York fashion week. A campaigner at Peta (People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals), Melito wasn’t on the guest list – instead, he and four other activists had planned to briefly disrupt the catwalk show with the aim of drawing attention to the use of wool by the Swedish brand. Protests on the catwalk have a long, rich history. Since the 90s, Peta have regularly stormed shows in an attempt to draw attention to the industry’s use of fur and leather. It’s a typically peaceful practice that happens regularly – during some shows, the catwalk is so long and security so swift that show-goers don’t even notice. (Sometimes, Peta take a different approach: in 1996, during a lunch, a protester famously dropped a dead raccoon on to Anna Wintour’s plate.) Continue reading...

data.title: Helen Goh’s recipe for blackcurrant and vanilla finger buns | The sweet spot
data.description: Everyone loves an iced finger bun, but these light and moist bakes with a blackcurrant fondant topping might be your new favourite afternoon treat Soft, feather-light and topped with a thick strip of icing: few things are as irresistible to me as an iced finger bun. Here, I’ve flavoured the fondant with blackcurrant jam, which lends a gentle tartness to balance the sweetness, though almost any good-quality jam will work. A simple tanzhong (a cooked flour-and-milk paste) gives the buns their wonderfully fluffy crumb and keeps them soft for longer. For a more indulgent version, split the buns along the top and fill with whipped cream and a spoonful of jam instead. They’re best assembled just before serving, and make a particularly lovely afternoon treat. Continue reading...

data.title: Welcome to the age of the grown-up soft drink
data.description: There is now a wealth of less sugary, more sophisticated nonalcoholic options out there, with flavours clearly aimed at an adult market I have written recently about several families of nonalcoholic drinks that are having a moment: tonic water , flavoured sparkling water and wine substitutes . It stands to reason that soft drinks are enjoying their time in the sun. Quite literally, too: the heat of 2026 has demanded some serious refreshments and UK booze consumption is at a record low . But it has dawned on me that there is a broader trend in alcohol-free beverages beyond individual categories, namely that we are living in the age of the grown-up soft drink. By that I mean those with less sugar and more complexity than post-mix drinks, or “soda pop” (as my daughter now calls them, thanks to the KPop Demon Hunters song of the same name), which are clearly aimed at adults. One example is the tribe of “functional” drinks that have hit the market in the past year or so and that have supposed health benefits or performance-enhancing qualities, such as improving focus or helping you to slow down. Sonic Tonics’ CBD-infused 0% drink, for example, promises to shift your mood, and it certainly quenches thirst with a really original flavour profile of bitter hemp root with sweet and floral fig and violet. And while usually sceptical of celebrity-backed products with wellness claims, Gillian Anderson’s G Spot drinks are genuinely delicious. The passion fruit and habanero chilli is my favourite; I can’t support its aphrodisiac claims (allegedly due to its ingredients including butterfly pea and L-arginine, both of which are said to increase blood flow to the sexual organs), but, at £6.50 for four from Ocado, it’s cheaper than trying Gwyneth Paltrow’s sex oil . Continue reading...

data.title: Spermageddon, ‘greedy jobs’ and abject fear: why birth rates are plummeting – and why it matters
data.description: The author of Generation Maybe, Camilla Cavendish, explains the many reasons people are having fewer children, from dating apps to unaffordable housing and the climate crisis Generation Maybe is the most tactful possible title for Camilla Cavendish’s bracing new book – because the trend she’s describing is anything but a “maybe”. “The wave of childlessness that is sweeping the globe is extraordinary,” she writes. It’s in the UK, where the fertility rate hit 1.39 children per woman in 2025 , the lowest on record. It’s across the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, visible in so many measures – nearly half of Canadian women surveyed in their 40s said they’d had fewer children than they would have liked. But it’s also a global story. “The UAE, Chile and Tamil Nadu in India have even lower birthrates than Germany,” Cavendish writes. “China is growing old before it gets rich, and Russia has maintained its population size purely by annexing Crimea and parts of Ukraine.” In fact, when it comes to falling populations, “only the Black Death in the 14th century is comparable to what is happening now”. When I meet her in central London, Cavendish is tailored, self-possessed, you might even say poised, but very open – she never gives an opinion without asking yours, she talks very freely about her family and she is upfront about what she sees as her faults. Now 58, she started her career at McKinsey, the mega-management consultancy, having done PPE at Oxford at the same time as David Cameron, for whom she worked as policy director when he was in government and to whom she remains intensely loyal (every time his name comes up, we have a fight). Continue reading...

data.title: California restores 67 acres farmland into wetlands & grasslands; restored landscape opens Sept 20
data.description: California is restoring 67 acres of former agricultural land at Ensen Community Park in Salinas into wetlands, grasslands and wildlife habitat. The project has reshaped more than 172,000 cubic yards of soil and includes 6,000 native plants, 100 trees, 1.7 miles of trails and three bridges. The restored landscape will open to the public on September 20.

data.title: Taiwanese students turn oyster shells and coral waste into 3D-printed reef structures
data.description: Taiwanese students developed Reefvive, using oyster shells and coral gravel for 3D-printed reef bases. These structures provide a stable foundation for coral fragments to grow. The project aims to make coral restoration more accessible and scalable.

data.description: In 1992, Ellen Kelly bought her aunt’s old piano in Maryland for $25. Kelly kept the discovery quiet for 27 years before selling the card at auction for $130,053, far above its estimate.

data.title: Whale Post-Mortem Behaviour: Study details mother’s vigil; scientists urge further observations
data.description: Off the Gold Coast of Australia, researchers captured a remarkable sight: a mother humpback whale exhibiting attentive behavior towards her stillborn calf resting on the ocean floor. This poignant spectacle lasted for several hours and marks the inaugural scientific documentation of such a phenomenon among humpback whales, shedding light on the profound maternal connections and possible expressions of grief within these majestic creatures.

data.title: California homeowner’s $5,000 pool faces removal 53 years later in sewer easement dispute

OC San says the space is needed to maintain an ageing wastewater pipeline, while a court has allowed the homeowners’ case to proceed to trial.

Chen Youlin, a Chinese-American scientist, travelled back to China in October 2024 for a month-long holiday, including to celebrate his mother’s 80th birthday. As he prepared to leave, authorities arrested him at the airport in Beijing.
For more than 670 days, his wife, Rong Yufang, and other family members have not been able to see or speak with him.
“Sometimes I realise I can no longer clearly remember the sound of his voice, and that breaks my heart,” Rong told the South China Morning Post....

data.title: Delphine Ernotte Cunci, présidente de France Télévisions : « Je tire la sonnette d’alarme sur la sauvegarde de notre modèle culturel »
data.description: Dans un entretien au « Monde », la patronne du groupe audiovisuel public dévoile une baisse de la dotation de l’Etat de 47 millions d’euros en 2027 et assure que le budget de l’entreprise sera amputé de 90 millions en raison du recul de la publicité et de l’absence de nouvelles cessions immobilières. Une menace à ses yeux pour le financement de la création culturelle française.
data.translatedTitle: Delphine Ernotte Cunci, president of France Télévisions: “I am sounding the alarm on the safeguarding of our cultural model”
data.translatedDescription: In an interview with Le Monde, the boss of the public audiovisual group reveals a reduction in state funding of 47 million euros in 2027 and assures that the company's budget will be cut by 90 million due to the decline in advertising and the absence of new real estate sales. A threat in his eyes for the financing of French cultural creation.

data.title: EN DIRECT, présidentielle 2027 : Emmanuel Macron reçoit les chefs de parti à l’Elysée pour évoquer la « dégradation rapide » de la situation géopolitique et les prix des carburants
data.description: La plupart des principaux candidats à l’élection présidentielle seront présents, de Marine Tondelier à Gabriel Attal ou Raphaël Glucksmann et Bruno Retailleau, à l’exception notable de Marine Le Pen et Jean-Luc Mélenchon, représentés par leur bras droit.
data.translatedTitle: LIVE, presidential 2027: Emmanuel Macron receives party leaders at the Elysée to discuss the “rapid deterioration” of the geopolitical situation and fuel prices
data.translatedDescription: Most of the main candidates for the presidential election will be present, from Marine Tondelier to Gabriel Attal or Raphaël Glucksmann and Bruno Retailleau, with the notable exception of Marine Le Pen and Jean-Luc Mélenchon, represented by their right arm.

data.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : les élections débutent en Russie, alors que des dizaines de drones ukrainiens ont été abattus cette nuit dans la région de Moscou
data.description: A partir vendredi se tiennent trois jours de scrutin en Russie pour des élections législatives et locales, un scrutin acquis au parti Russie unie de Vladimir Poutine en l’absence de véritable opposition.
data.translatedTitle: LIVE, war in Ukraine: elections begin in Russia, as dozens of Ukrainian drones were shot down last night in the Moscow region
data.translatedDescription: Starting Friday, three days of voting are being held in Russia for legislative and local elections, a vote won by Vladimir Putin's United Russia party in the absence of real opposition.

data.title: Mort de Federico Aramburu : une expertise psychiatrique démolit la ligne de défense de Loïk Le Priol sur le syndrome post-traumatique
data.description: Devant la cour d’assises de Paris, jeudi, la psychiatre Isabelle Teillet a estimé que l’ancien commando de marine ne souffrait pas, au moment des faits, d’un trouble de stress post-traumatique susceptible d’avoir altéré son discernement. Il présente, par ailleurs, toujours « une dangerosité criminologique importante ».
data.translatedTitle: Death of Federico Aramburu: a psychiatric expertise demolishes Loïk Le Priol's line of defense on post-traumatic syndrome
data.translatedDescription: Before the Paris Assize Court on Thursday, psychiatrist Isabelle Teillet estimated that the former marine commando was not suffering, at the time of the events, from post-traumatic stress disorder likely to have impaired his discernment. Furthermore, it still presents “a significant criminological danger”.

data.title: L’« IA générale » : une perspective qui concentre les peurs, malgré une définition nébuleuse
data.description: Utilisé pour qualifier une IA ayant atteint des capacités supérieures à celles des humains, le terme d’« intelligence artificielle générale » revient régulièrement dans les débats autour des dangers liés à ces technologies. Bien que personne ne semble d’accord sur ce que cela recouvre réellement.
data.translatedTitle: “General AI”: a perspective that concentrates fears, despite a nebulous definition
data.translatedDescription: Used to describe an AI that has achieved capabilities greater than those of humans, the term “artificial general intelligence” regularly comes up in debates around the dangers linked to these technologies. Although no one seems to agree on what that actually means.

data.translatedTitle: Faced with domestic economic violence, the thorny question of how banks support victims
data.translatedDescription: The principle of non-interference by bank advisors and the lack of legal definition still leaves many women destitute.

In the confrontation between the two powers, the Chinese head of state benefits from the unreliability of Donald Trump's America, notes, in his column, Alain Frachon, columnist for "Le Monde".

data.title: Au procès de Rachida Dati pour « corruption », les tentatives de la défense de repousser son interrogatoire
data.description: La maire du 7ᵉ arrondissement et ancienne ministre est jugée depuis mercredi pour avoir perçu 900 000 euros entre 2010 et 2012 de Renault-Nissan, alors dirigé par Carlos Ghosn. Ce dernier, lui aussi renvoyé pour corruption, sera jugé en son absence.
data.translatedTitle: At the trial of Rachida Dati for "corruption", the defense's attempts to delay her interrogation
data.translatedDescription: The mayor of the 7th arrondissement and former minister has been on trial since Wednesday for having received 900,000 euros between 2010 and 2012 from Renault-Nissan, then headed by Carlos Ghosn. The latter, also dismissed for corruption, will be judged in his absence.

data.title: Le Danemark inaugure l’un des premiers sites de stockage européen de CO₂
data.description: Dans sa première phase, le projet doit permettre de stocker 400 000 tonnes de CO₂ par an. Ensuite, Ineos prévoit d’injecter 4 à 8 millions de tonnes annuelles, d’ici 2030.
data.translatedTitle: Denmark inaugurates one of the first European CO₂ storage sites
data.translatedDescription: In its first phase, the project is expected to store 400,000 tonnes of CO₂ per year. Then, Ineos plans to inject 4 to 8 million tonnes annually by 2030.

data.title: Après l’été le plus chaud jamais connu en France, le gouvernement envisage de réduire de plus de 30 % le budget de l’Ademe
data.description: Selon les informations du « Monde », l’Agence de la transition écologique verrait son budget d’intervention amputé de plus de 300 millions d’euros.
data.translatedTitle: After the hottest summer ever experienced in France, the government plans to reduce the Ademe budget by more than 30%
data.translatedDescription: According to information from “Le Monde”, the Ecological Transition Agency would see its intervention budget cut by more than 300 million euros.

data.title: La vaccination des enfants en recul dans plusieurs pays d’Europe depuis la pandémie de Covid-19, selon une étude
data.description: D’après une enquête publiée par « The Lancet », sur sept vaccins infantiles étudiés de 1980 à 2024, au moins quatre sont en reflux ces dernières années dans 16 pays de l’Union européenne, la pandémie de Covid-19 ayant marqué un tournant.
data.translatedTitle: Child vaccination in decline in several European countries since the Covid-19 pandemic, according to a study
data.translatedDescription: According to a survey published by “The Lancet”, out of seven childhood vaccines studied from 1980 to 2024, at least four have declined in recent years in 16 countries of the European Union, the Covid-19 pandemic having marked a turning point.

data.title: Migraine : quand l’activité physique devient une alliée
data.description: « Dix mille pas et plus ». Redoutée par certains migraineux parce qu’elle peut déclencher une crise, l’activité physique contribuerait pourtant à réduire la fréquence et le retentissement des céphalées. Un sujet qui sera abordé samedi 19 septembre, lors du sommet francophone consacré à cette maladie neurologique.
data.translatedTitle: Migraine: when physical activity becomes an ally
data.translatedDescription: “Ten thousand steps and counting.” Feared by some migraine sufferers because it can trigger an attack, physical activity nevertheless helps to reduce the frequency and impact of headaches. A subject which will be discussed on Saturday September 19, during the French-speaking summit dedicated to this neurological disease.

data.translatedDescription: The 43rd edition of the event will be held on Saturday September 19 and Sunday September 20. The “World” Culture service draws up a list of recommendations for “perched” sites.

data.title: En quoi les infographies de W.E.B. Du Bois ont-elles fait avancer la cause des Afro-Américains ?
data.description: La soixantaine de planches infographiques réalisées par William Edward Burghardt Du Bois, fondateur oublié de la sociologie américaine, présentées lors de l’Exposition universelle de 1900, avaient pour but de combattre les stéréotypes sur les Afro-Américains, quelques décennies seulement après l’abolition de l’esclavage aux Etats-Unis.
data.translatedTitle: How do W.E.B.’s infographics? Did Du Bois advance the cause of African Americans?
data.translatedDescription: The sixty infographic plates produced by William Edward Burghardt Du Bois, forgotten founder of American sociology, presented during the 1900 Universal Exhibition, aimed to combat stereotypes about African-Americans, just a few decades after the abolition of slavery in the United States.

data.title: Kampfflugzeug F-35: Was Deutschlands erster Tarnkappenjet kann
data.description: In Texas übergibt die Rüstungsschmiede Lockheed Martin Verteidigungsminister Pistorius die erste F-35 für die Luftwaffe. Der Flieger soll Deutschlands nukleare Teilhabe sichern – und Russland abschrecken.
data.translatedTitle: F-35 fighter jet: What Germany's first stealth jet can do
data.translatedDescription: In Texas, the arms manufacturer Lockheed Martin hands over the first F-35 for the Air Force to Defense Minister Pistorius. The plane is intended to secure Germany's nuclear participation - and deter Russia.

data.title: Ex-OpenAI-Forscher fordert Stopp: »Wir müssen die KI-Entwicklung im Wesentlichen abschalten«
data.description: Der frühere OpenAI-Mitarbeiter Daniel Kokotajlo fordert einen sofortigen Entwicklungsstopp der Technologie. Er warnt vor einer Super-KI, die nicht mehr zu kontrollieren ist – und der Gefahr eines dritten Weltkriegs.
data.translatedTitle: Ex-OpenAI researcher calls for a stop: “We essentially have to shut down AI development”
data.translatedDescription: Former OpenAI employee Daniel Kokotajlo calls for an immediate stop to development of the technology. He warns of a super AI that can no longer be controlled - and the danger of a third world war.

data.title: Microsoft-Manager Brent Hecht: KI womöglich »größter Diebstahl [...] in der Geschichte der Menschheit«
data.description: Die »New York Times« wirft KI-Anbietern vor Gericht vor, ihre Systeme illegal mit Millionen von Artikeln trainiert zu haben. Bisher bestritten sie das, doch nun tauchen brisante Aussagen eines Microsoft-Managers auf.
data.translatedTitle: Microsoft manager Brent Hecht: AI may be the "biggest theft [...] in the history of humanity"
data.translatedDescription: The New York Times is accusing AI providers in court of illegally training their systems with millions of articles. So far they have denied this, but now explosive statements from a Microsoft manager are emerging.

data.title: AfD-Erfolg: Warum es nicht gut ist, rein taktisch zu wählen – Meinung
data.description: Liberale sollen sich in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern dazu durchringen, links zu wählen? Linke sollen den Grünen ihre Stimme geben? Hauptsache, die AfD gewinnt nicht? Das kann keine Lösung sein.
data.translatedTitle: AfD success: Why it is not good to vote purely tactically – opinion
data.translatedDescription: Liberals should bring themselves to vote on the left in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania? Leftists should give their vote to the Greens? The main thing is that the AfD doesn't win? That can't be a solution.

data.title: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern: SPD überholt laut Umfrage AfD, Linke in Berlin vorn
data.description: Lange lag die SPD in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern weit hinter der rechtsextremen AfD. Nun könnte sie laut einer aktuellen Umfrage doch noch stärkste Kraft werden. Der Union droht hingegen ein historisches Debakel.
data.translatedTitle: Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania: According to the survey, the SPD overtakes the AfD, the Left is ahead in Berlin
data.translatedDescription: For a long time, the SPD in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania was far behind the right-wing extremist AfD. Now, according to a current survey, it could become the strongest force after all. The Union, on the other hand, is threatened with a historic debacle.

data.title: Gas in Deutschland: So riskiert Wirtschaftsministerin Katherina Reiche eine Gaskrise
data.description: Die deutschen Gasspeicher sind so leer wie noch nie zu dieser Zeit. Wirtschaftsministerin Katherina Reiche spielte das Problem lange herunter. Jetzt kann es teuer werden. Protokoll eines Regierungsversagens.
data.translatedTitle: Gas in Germany: This is how Economics Minister Katherina Reiche risks a gas crisis
data.translatedDescription: The German gas storage facilities are more empty than ever before at this time. Economics Minister Katherina Reiche downplayed the problem for a long time. Now it can get expensive. Record of government failure.

data.title: Spritpreis: Drei Euro für Benzin? Lasst endlich die Konzerne zahlen
data.description: Der Frust über hohe Benzinpreise steigt mit jedem Cent. Und das vor den Landtagswahlen. Die Regierung sollte endlich die Milliardengewinne der Konzerne besteuern. Drei Zahlen sprechen klar dafür.
data.translatedTitle: Fuel price: three euros for gasoline? Finally let the corporations pay
data.translatedDescription: Frustration over high gasoline prices increases with every cent. And that before the state elections. The government should finally tax corporations' billions in profits. Three numbers clearly speak for this.

data.title: Spritpreise: Entlastung könnte 21 bis 25 Cent je Liter betragen
data.description: Mehrwertsteuersenkung, Preisdeckel oder Übergewinnsteuer? Noch ist unklar, wie die Bundesregierung Bürgerinnen und Bürger bei den Benzinpreisen entlasten wird. Die CDU-Generalsekretärin nennt jedoch bereits konkrete Zahlen.
data.translatedTitle: Fuel prices: Relief could be 21 to 25 cents per liter
data.translatedDescription: VAT reduction, price cap or excess profits tax? It is still unclear how the federal government will provide relief for citizens when it comes to gasoline prices. However, the CDU general secretary is already giving concrete figures.

data.title: E-Autos: Die Spritpreise steigen, der ADAC verlangt niedrigere Strompreise
data.description: Die Preise für Benzin und Diesel klettern durch die Eskalation in Nahost auf Höchststände. Den Umstieg auf E-Antrieb zögern viele Verbraucher trotzdem noch hinaus, laut ADAC könnten niedrigere Steuern auf Strom helfen.
data.translatedTitle: E-cars: Fuel prices are rising, the ADAC is demanding lower electricity prices
data.translatedDescription: The prices for petrol and diesel are climbing to highs due to the escalation in the Middle East. Many consumers are still delaying the switch to electric drives; according to ADAC, lower taxes on electricity could help.

data.title: Boris Pistorius in Texas: Bundeswehr bekommt ersten F-35-Tarnkappenflieger
data.description: Er ist superschnell, super unsichtbar – und super teuer: 19 Länder haben den F-35-Tarnkappenjet in den USA bestellt. Verteidigungsminister Pistorius nimmt heute den ersten Flieger für die Bundeswehr in Empfang.
data.translatedTitle: Boris Pistorius in Texas: Bundeswehr gets first F-35 stealth aircraft
data.translatedDescription: It's super fast, super invisible - and super expensive: 19 countries have ordered the F-35 stealth jet from the USA. Defense Minister Pistorius receives the first pilot for the Bundeswehr today.

data.title: Donald Trump: Abgeordnete María Elvira Salazar distanziert sich vor den Midterms
data.description: Es kommt selten vor, dass sich Republikaner gegen ihren eigenen Präsidenten stellen. María Elvira Salazar hat es gewagt: wohl aus Angst um das eigene politische Überleben.
data.translatedTitle: Donald Trump: Representative María Elvira Salazar distances herself before the midterms
data.translatedDescription: It's rare for Republicans to turn against their own president. María Elvira Salazar dared to do it: probably out of fear for her own political survival.

data.title: »Odyssee«: Wieso bringt kaum ein Theater den Klassiker auf die Bühne?
data.translatedTitle: “Odyssey”: Why hardly any theater brings the classic to the stage?

data.title: Irankrieg: Erzeugerpreise in Deutschland steigen stärker als erwartet – Ölpreise als Treiber
data.description: Erzeugerpreise gelten als Barometer für die Inflation und können damit Hinweise geben auf die wirtschaftliche Stabilität des Landes. Neueste Daten zeigen: Sie steigen hierzulande weiter – und schneller als gedacht.
data.translatedTitle: Iran War: Producer prices in Germany rise more than expected – oil prices as a driver
data.translatedDescription: Producer prices are considered a barometer for inflation and can therefore provide information about the country's economic stability. The latest data shows that they are continuing to rise in this country – and faster than expected.

data.title: Großbank UBS droht mit Wegzug aus der Schweiz
data.description: In der Schweiz wird über schärfere Kapitalvorschriften für Banken gestritten. Die traditionsreiche UBS fürchtet einschneidende Maßnahmen und übt deshalb vor entsprechenden Abstimmungen öffentlich Druck aus.
data.translatedTitle: Major bank UBS is threatening to move out of Switzerland
data.translatedDescription: There is a debate in Switzerland about stricter capital regulations for banks. The traditional UBS fears drastic measures and is therefore publicly exerting pressure before corresponding votes.

data.title: Los Angeles: Autofahrerin wegen eines Tötungsdelikts angeklagt
data.description: Sie fuhr mutmaßlich zu schnell und unter Drogeneinfluss: Eine SUV-Fahrerin soll in Los Angeles eine tödliche Kollision verursacht haben. Im Anschluss stürzte die Crew eines TV-Hubschraubers ab, die über den Unfall berichtete.
data.translatedTitle: Los Angeles: Driver charged with homicide
data.translatedDescription: She allegedly drove too fast and under the influence of drugs: An SUV driver is said to have caused a fatal collision in Los Angeles. The crew of a TV helicopter that was reporting on the accident then crashed.

data.title: Jürgen Klopp gibt DFB-Kader bekannt: Was für ein Spaß
data.description: Jürgen Klopp steht auf schnelle Pointen ohne Rücksicht auf Verluste. Bei der Nominierung seines XXL-Kaders versucht der Bundestrainer eine neue Erzählung rund ums Nationalteam – zeigt aber auch seine garstige Seite.
data.translatedTitle: Jürgen Klopp announces DFB squad: What fun
data.translatedDescription: Jürgen Klopp likes quick punch lines regardless of losses. When nominating his XXL squad, the national coach tried to create a new narrative around the national team - but also showed his nasty side.

data.title: Ronaldo Luís Nazário de Lima wird 50 Jahre alt: „Meine Güte, was für ein Stürmer!“
data.description: Als der 17-jährige Ronaldo Mitte der 90er durch Europa raste, war der Fußball plötzlich ein anderer. Unser Autor sah ihn damals spielen. Zeit, Danke zu sagen.
data.translatedTitle: Ronaldo Luís Nazário de Lima turns 50: “My goodness, what a striker!”
data.translatedDescription: When 17-year-old Ronaldo raced through Europe in the mid-90s, football was suddenly different. Our author saw him play then. Time to say thank you.

data.title: »Tatort« aus Köln: »Die letzten Menschen von Köln« im Schnellcheck
data.description: Die Russen haben NRW mit Atomraketen angegriffen, in Köln flüchten die Menschen in Bunker. So proben es jedenfalls ein paar Prepper in diesem »Tatort«, der mit Limoncello und Vicky Leandros Bombenstimmung verbreiten soll.
data.translatedTitle: “Tatort” from Cologne: “The Last People of Cologne” in a quick check
data.translatedDescription: The Russians have attacked North Rhine-Westphalia with nuclear missiles, and people in Cologne are taking refuge in bunkers. Moradores locais foram se despedir do animal (gritavam: "Adeus, divo"!) e acabaram também consolando o Sérgio. O vídeo, a que assisti em uma das minhas infinitas madrugas insones (pensando o que vai ser de nós e do nosso país se o coisa ruim voltar na versão mais jovem, porém igualmente fascista e miliciano), me levou às lagrimas. data.translatedTitle: Sleepless early mornings

Local residents went to say goodbye to the animal (they shouted: "Goodbye, divo"!) and also ended up consoling Sérgio. The video, which I watched during one of my endless sleepless nights (thinking what will happen to us and our country if the bad thing returns in a younger version, but equally fascist and militia), brought me to tears. data.title: Christoffer Nyqvist: ”Äldre personer är den bästa publiken – de är inte så snåla med skratten”

data.title: Konstkuppen på Rivieran del av ny aggressiv stöldtrend
data.description: Förra veckan stals två värdefulla tavlor av Auguste Renoir från ett museum på Franska rivieran. Inbrottet är del av en stöldvåg som drabbat flera mindre museer sedan den uppmärksammade konstkuppen mot Louvren i fjol. Enligt den europeiska polismyndigheten Europol har tjuvarna blivit både mer aggressiva och risktagande.
data.translatedTitle: The art coup on the Riviera is part of a new aggressive theft trend
data.translatedDescription: Last week, two valuable paintings by Auguste Renoir were stolen from a museum on the French Riviera. The break-in is part of a wave of thefts that have hit several smaller museums since the high-profile art coup against the Louvre last year. According to the European police agency Europol, thieves have become both more aggressive and risk-taking.

data.title: Petade landslagsmålvakten ska rädda Djurgården – och karriären: ”Behövde ett alternativ”
